question.problem: Let $P=\{{z}_{0},{z}_{1},…,{z}_{q}\}$ be a partition of the interval $[4,9].$ If $Δ{z}_{k}={z}_{k}-{z}_{k-1},$ calculate ${\sum }_{k=1}^{q}7Δ{z}_{k}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we take the factor $7$ outside the summation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{k=1}^{q}7Δ{z}_{k}=7{\sum }_{k=1}^{q}Δ{z}_{k}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that ${\sum }_{k=1}^{q}Δ{z}_{k}$ is just the length of the interval $[4,9],$ because

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{k=1}^{q}Δ{z}_{k} & =({z}_{1}-{z}_{0})+({z}_{2}-{z}_{1})+({z}_{3}-{z}_{2})+⋯+({z}_{q}-{z}_{q-1}) \\  & =(\cancel{{z}_{1}}-{z}_{0})+(\cancel{{z}_{2}}-\cancel{{z}_{1}})+(\cancel{{z}_{3}}-\cancel{{z}_{2}})+⋯+({z}_{q}-\cancel{{z}_{q-1}}) \\  & =-{z}_{0}+{z}_{q} \\  & ={z}_{q}-{z}_{0} \\  & =9-4 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
7{\sum }_{k=1}^{q}Δ{z}_{k}=7\cdot 5=35.
$$
